profile.name: Ledgerly Inc.
profile.summary: US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). Small-business invoicing. No lending, no securities brokerage, not a bank.
businessLines: Prepaid / debit card program via sponsor bank
applies: Bank Secrecy Act / AML, FinCEN rules for MSBs, Travel Rule, CVC rules
OFAC sanctions screening (customers and counterparties, incl. crypto addresses)
CFPB rules: Reg E (EFTA), remittance rule, prepaid rule, UDAAP, larger-participant rules for payment apps
Consumer data privacy / GLBA, open banking (1033)
FTC consumer protection that touches payment apps
Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets
doesNotApply: SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets
Sanctions actions only matter via the screening program, not individually

aml-bsa.description: AML/BSA program, FinCEN, Travel Rule, SARs

consumer-payments.description: Reg E, remittances, prepaid, CFPB supervision, UDAAP

prompts.jevQuestion: Would the general counsel of this company need to know about this federal document because it could create, change or remove a compliance obligation or material legal risk for the company's actual business lines? Routine filings for other industries are not relevant.
prompts.extractSystem: Extract every dated obligation or deadline (comment due, effective, compliance) stated in the text. Quote the sentence verbatim. If none, return an empty list.
prompts.actionsSystem: Write one action item per document for a busy general counsel: an imperative sentence (≤ 25 words) saying what the owner should do and why, in plain English a non-lawyer understands — spell out acronyms, no regulatory jargon. Do NOT write any dates or citations — those are rendered separately from verified data.
prompts.webLeadsSystem: You find leads on new US federal regulatory actions. Search, then list the URLs you found. Do not summarise law from memory.
prompts.webLeadsPrompt:
{{profile}}

Find US federal regulatory developments (final rules, proposed rules, guidance, enforcement) published {{windowStart}} to {{windowEnd}} that could affect this company. Run at most 3 searches. Reply with the URLs only.
prompts.panelJudge:
You are one judge on a panel grading action items that a General Counsel would forward to a colleague.
For EVERY item and EVERY listed criterion, answer PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN (UNKNOWN only if the item gives you too little to decide), with a one-line reason.
Judge only the criterion asked. Do not judge whether the rule is truly relevant to the company — that is graded elsewhere.
Each item is a card as the reader sees it: the action text plus "datesShown" (verified dates displayed next to the action) and "tier". Action texts deliberately contain no dates, so a date the rubric mentions counts as covered when it appears in "datesShown".
For "covers", a paraphrase that conveys the business-relevant substance counts; exact names, populations and sub-details are not required.

Criteria:
{{criteria}}

Items (a "rubric" is present only when the answer key has one for that item):
{{items}}

question: Would the general counsel of this company need to know about this federal document because it could create, change or remove a compliance obligation or material legal risk for the company's actual business lines? Routine filings for other industries are not relevant.
state:
Company: Ledgerly Inc.

US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). Small-business invoicing. No lending, no securities brokerage, not a bank.

Rules that APPLY:
- Bank Secrecy Act / AML, FinCEN rules for MSBs, Travel Rule, CVC rules
- OFAC sanctions screening (customers and counterparties, incl. crypto addresses)
- CFPB rules: Reg E (EFTA), remittance rule, prepaid rule, UDAAP, larger-participant rules for payment apps
- Consumer data privacy / GLBA, open banking (1033)
- FTC consumer protection that touches payment apps
- Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
- Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
- CFTC derivatives market rules (DCMs, swaps)
- Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets
- Sanctions actions only matter via the screening program, not individually

This AD requires revising the ALS of the existing approved engine maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive tasks and limitations and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

[2026-21299] Rule — Interior Department; National Park Service
Title: Alaska; Wildlife, Harvest, and Access
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The National Park Service (NPS) amends its regulations for hunting, fishing, trapping, and other harvest-related activities in Alaska and the procedures used to restrict public use and access in Alaska park areas, including for subsistence. This rule restores the regulatory framework adopted to implement the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act of 1980 (ANILCA) in 1981 that guided management for more than three decades, with targeted updates to that framework in response to public comments and further agency review. The restored framework recognizes the complementary and distinct roles of the State of Alaska, the Federal Subsistence Management Program, and the NPS in managing public uses and resources in Alaska park areas. The rule removes regulatory changes made in 2015, 2017, and 2024 that departed from that framework. These amendments are consistent with Executive Orders 14153 and 14192 and Secretary of the Interior's Orders 3422 and 3447.

[2026-21319] Rule — Personnel Management Office
Title: Elimination of Time-in-Grade
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is adopting, substantially as proposed, its proposed rule eliminating the Time-in- Grade (TIG) restriction on advancement to competitive service positions in the General Schedule (GS). Under the prior regulations, a candidate generally could not be advanced to a covered position at GS-6 or above without completing 52 weeks in a position no more than one grade lower--or two grades lower for certain positions in two-grade-interval lines of work. This final rule removes that requirement. Employees remain subject to all applicable occupational qualification standards and any additional job-related qualification requirements established by their employing agency.

Company: Ledgerly Inc.

US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). - Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
- Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
- CFTC derivatives market rules (DCMs, swaps)
- Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets

[2026-21330] Notice — Defense Department; Defense Acquisition Regulations System
Title: Information Collection Requirement; Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) Parts 223 and 226, Occupational Safety and Drug-Free Work Force
Action: Notice and request for comments regarding a proposed extension of an approved information collection requirement.
Abstract: In compliance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, DoD announces the proposed extension of a public information collection requirement and seeks public comment on the provisions thereof. DoD invites comments on: whether the proposed collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of DoD, including whether the information will have practical utility; the accuracy of DoD's estimate of the burden of the proposed information collection; ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and ways to minimize the burden of the information collection on respondents, including through the use of automated collection techniques or other forms of information technology. DoD proposes that OMB approve an extension of the information collection requirement, to expire three years after the approval date.

[2026-21334] Proposed Rule — Transportation Department; Federal Aviation Administration
Title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
Action: Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).
Abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-09-07, which applies to certain Airbus SAS Model A330-243, -243F, -841, and -941 airplanes. AD 2025-09-07 requires revising the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) by providing instructions to address dual loss of radio management panel (RMP) data synchronization, and the existing minimum equipment list (MEL) by removing relief for an inoperative RMP 3. Since the FAA issued AD 2025-09-07, a modification that addresses the unsafe condition has been developed. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions specified in AD 2025-09-07 and would require modifying the airplane. This proposed AD also reduces the applicability. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

Title: Interpretation of “Flammable Liquid Fuels” With Respect to Fuel Additives

[2026-21347] Proposed Rule — Federal Communications Commission
Title: Modernizing the Commission's National Environmental Policy Act Rules
Action: Proposed rule.
Abstract: In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) seeks additional comment on the Commission's National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA) framework, to further expedite, simplify, and reduce the costs of environmental review. This includes refreshing the record on the meaning of "undertaking" and the Commission's approach to implementing section 106 of the NHPA. The Commission also seeks comment on whether activities related to the deployment and operation of communications infrastructure are within the scope of "undertaking," as well as on other practices or actions the Commission could adopt to provide more efficiency and predictability in the section 106 process. Additionally, the Commission seeks comment on whether communications infrastructure deployments are agency actions subject to the Endangered Species Act (ESA).

Action: Final rule.
Abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), in response to a request under the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA) of 1972 from the Alaska Oil and Gas Association (AOGA), finalize regulations facilitating the authorization of incidental, unintentional take of small numbers of polar bears (Ursus maritimus) and Pacific walruses (Odobenus rosmarus divergens) during year-round oil and gas industry activities in the Beaufort Sea (Alaska and the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS)) and adjacent northern coast of Alaska. [2026-21387] Proposed Rule — Transportation Department; Federal Aviation Administration
Title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
Action: Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).
Abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Model AS350B3, AS355F, AS355F1, AS355F2, AS355N, AS355NP, EC130B4, and EC130T2 helicopters. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of the loss of the tightening torque between the upper ball bearing end and a main rotor (MR) servo-control. This proposed AD would require an inspection of the nut tightening torque of the upper ball bearing end of all the MR servo-controls and, depending on the results, corrective actions. The proposed AD would also require reporting the inspection results. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

Title: Joint Application Package From the State of Utah to the Surface Transportation Project Delivery Program and Proposed Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) Assigning Environmental Responsibilities to the State
Action: Notice, request for comments.
Abstract: This notice announces that FRA and FTA (Agencies) have received and reviewed an application package from the State of Utah (State), Utah Department of Transportation (UDOT), requesting participation in the Surface Transportation Project Delivery Program (Program). Under the Program, the Agencies may assign, and a State may assume, responsibilities under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), and all or part of the Agencies' responsibilities for environmental review, consultation, or other actions required under any Federal environmental laws except certain statutory exclusions with respect to one or more railroad projects and one or more public transportation projects within the State. The Agencies have determined the application package to be complete and developed a draft Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the State outlining how UDOT will implement the Program with the Agencies' oversight. The public is invited to comment on UDOT's request, including its application package and the proposed MOU, which includes the proposed assignments and assumptions of environmental review, consultation, and other activities.

[2026-21450] Rule — Commerce Department; National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
Title: Atlantic Highly Migratory Species; Atlantic Bluefin Tuna Fisheries; Closure of the General Category October Through November Fishery for 2026
Action: Temporary rule; closure.
Abstract: NMFS closes the General category fishery for Atlantic bluefin tuna (BFT) for the remainder of the October through November time period. The General category may only retain, possess, or land large medium and giant (i.e., measuring 73 inches (185 centimeters (cm) curved fork length (CFL) or greater) BFT when the fishery is open. This action also waives the previously scheduled restricted-fishing days (RFDs) for the remainder of the October through November time period. With the RFDs waived during the closure, fishermen aboard General category permitted vessels and HMS Charter/Headboat permitted vessels may tag and release BFT of all sizes, subject to the requirements of the catch-and-release and tag-and-release programs. On December 1, 2026, the fishery will reopen automatically.

[2026-21491] Notice — Health and Human Services Department; Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
Title: Privacy Act of 1974; Matching Program
Action: Notice of a new matching program.
Abstract: In accordance with subsection (e)(12) of the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), is providing notice of a computer matching program between CMS and the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA). The purpose of the matching program is to identify beneficiaries enrolled in both Medicare and VHA health care and to identify medical claims for which both agencies made payment for the same health care services. Under this agreement, the VHA will provide CMS with a finder file on a recurring basis, of all Veteran beneficiaries enrolled in VHA health care that CMS will use to identify dually enrolled beneficiaries. CMS and VHA will use the results of the matching program to recover duplicate payments, improve payment accuracy, and identify potential fraud, waste, and abuse.

[2026-21507] Proposed Rule — Commerce Department; National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
Title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Modify Groundfish Season Timing in the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands and Gulf of Alaska Groundfish Fisheries
Action: Proposed rule; request for comments.
Abstract: NMFS proposes two technical revisions to regulations for the opening and closing times of groundfish fisheries in the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands (BSAI) and Gulf of Alaska (GOA) management areas. First, this proposed rule would authorize NMFS to determine the opening and closing times for the sablefish Individual Fishing Quota (IFQ) and Community Development Quota (CDQ) fishing season, taking into consideration the halibut IFQ/CDQ season set by the International Pacific Halibut Commission (IPHC). Second, this proposed rule would allow NMFS flexibility to change the time of day for closing a groundfish fishery. This proposed rule is necessary to minimize regulatory discards, reduce uncertainty for fishery participants, and enable fuller utilization and more precise limitation of allowable harvest. This action is intended to promote the goals and objectives of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson- Stevens Act), the Fishery Management Plan for the Groundfish of the BSAI Management Area (BSAI FMP) and the Fishery Management Plan for the Groundfish Fisheries of the GOA (GOA FMP), and other applicable laws.

[2026-21512] Proposed Rule — National Credit Union Administration
Title: Notification to Members/Shareholders
Action: Proposed rule.
Abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) solicits public comment on a proposal to streamline the methods a federally insured credit union (FICU) may use to provide its members with notice of share insurance coverage. The current regulation is overly prescriptive, mandating that a FICU make available hard copies of certain prescribed materials. While a FICU would still be required to provide notice to members, the proposed rule would defer to the FICU on the method used for such notification. Among other methods, a FICU may elect to provide members with a link to updated online resources that will be maintained on the NCUA website. The Board believes the proposed rule will provide greater flexibility, reduce compliance costs for both NCUA and FICUs, and ensure that members are provided with up-to-date information regarding share insurance coverage.

Company: Ledgerly Inc.

US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). Small-business invoicing. No lending, no securities brokerage, not a bank.

Rules that APPLY:
- Bank Secrecy Act / AML, FinCEN rules for MSBs, Travel Rule, CVC rules
- OFAC sanctions screening (customers and counterparties, incl. crypto addresses)
- CFPB rules: Reg E (EFTA), remittance rule, prepaid rule, UDAAP, larger-participant rules for payment apps
- Consumer data privacy / GLBA, open banking (1033)
- FTC consumer protection that touches payment apps
- Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
- Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
- CFTC derivatives market rules (DCMs, swaps)
- Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets
- Sanctions actions only matter via the screening program, not individually

[2026-21697] Notice — Veterans Affairs Department
Title: Privacy Act of 1974; System of Records
Action: Notice of a modified system of records.
Abstract: As required by the Privacy Act of 1974, notice is hereby given that VA is modifying an existing system of records titled, "Veterans and Uniformed Services Personnel Programs of U.S. Government Life Insurance--VA" (36VA29). This system is housed within a cloud-based computer system called "Life Insurance Policy Administration Solution" (LIPAS), which is a managed service solution leveraging commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software applications hosted in the VA Enterprise Cloud Amazon Web Services GovCloud (VAEC-AWS) High environment. LIPAS replaced the retired Insurance Payment System mainframe and Veterans Insurance Claim Tracking and Response System (VICTARS). By using LIPAS to integrate with VA Enterprise shared services, LIPAS provides the components necessary for VA Insurance policy administration and management.

[2026-21705] Notice — Treasury Department; Comptroller of the Currency
Title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Proposed Information Collection; Submission for OMB Review; Reporting Forms and Instructions for Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers Subject to the Jurisdiction of the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
Action: Notice and request for comment.
Abstract: The OCC, as part of its continuing effort to reduce paperwork and respondent burden, invites comment on a new information collection, as required by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA). In accordance with the requirements of the PRA, the OCC may not conduct or sponsor, and the respondent is not required to respond to an information collection unless it displays a currently valid Office of Management and Budget (OMB) control number. The OCC is proposing a new information collection titled "Reporting Forms and Instructions for Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers Subject to the Jurisdiction of the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency," that would include weekly and quarterly reporting forms that must be completed by permitted payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers. The OCC is seeking a new OMB control number for this information collection. The OCC also is giving notice that it has sent the collection to OMB for review.

Abstract: Service's (IRS) currently accepted burden estimate methodology, referred to as the RAAS Taxpayer Burden Model, is based on taxpayers' tax reporting experience taking into account, among other things, the forms and schedules used by those taxpayers and the recordkeeping and other activities needed to complete those forms. The transition of the information return \1\ reporting burden represents the IRS's continued effort to improve the ability of IRS to measure the burden imposed on various groups of taxpayers by the Federal tax system. While the RAAS Taxpayer Burden Model methodology provides a more accurate and comprehensive description of information return reporting burden, it will not provide burden estimates on a form-by-form basis, as has been done under the previous methodology. When the prior model, known as the legacy Arthur D. Little (ADL) model was developed in the mid-1980s, almost all tax returns were prepared manually, either by the taxpayer or a paid preparer. In this context, it was determined that estimating burden on a form-by-form, line-by- line basis was an appropriate methodology. The RAAS Taxpayer Burden Model methodology relies on surveys that gather data about time spent and out-of-pocket costs incurred for pre-issuing and issuing activities for information return issuers. The methodology establishes econometric relationships between tax return characteristics and reported compliance costs. The methodology controls for the substitution of time and money by monetizing time and reporting total compliance costs in dollars. The RAAS Taxpayer Burden Model methodology better reflects taxpayer compliance burden because, in a world of electronic tax preparation, time and out-of-pockets costs are governed by the information required rather than the form on which it is ultimately reported. Importantly, even where various information return issuers complete the same tax form lines, the RAAS Taxpayer Burden Model methodology differentiates the cost incurred to complete those forms based on characteristics of those issuers. Effect on Cost of Short-Term Treasury Debt Financing The OCC anticipates that the final rule will benefit the U.S. government and taxpayers by increasing the demand for short-term Treasury debt securities. Because research suggests that short-term Treasury securities do not have close substitutes, an increase in demand for these securities would be expected to lower short-term Treasury yields. [2026-21267] Rule — Treasury Department; Internal Revenue Service
Title: Regulations Regarding Payment of Tax by Commercially Acceptable Means
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: December 14, 2001, authorizes payment of internal revenue taxes by credit or debit card so long as such payments are made in the manner and in accordance with the forms, instructions, and procedures prescribed by the Commissioner of Internal Revenue (Commissioner). Prior to passage of the TFA, section 6311(d)(2) authorized the Secretary to enter into contracts to obtain services related to receiving payment of taxes by credit card or debit card, or charge card, but prohibited the Secretary from paying any fee or other consideration under any such contract. Existing Sec. 301.6311-2(f) implements this provision. Existing Sec. 301.6311-2(e) prohibits the IRS from imposing any fee or charge on persons making payment of taxes by credit card or debit card. You are an in-house regulatory analyst triaging the Federal Register for one company. Be strict: mark relevant only if the document itself creates, changes or removes something this company (or its direct suppliers or customers) must do, pay, stop or decide.
Mark NOT relevant when the document:
- covers a different product, model, plant, industry or place than the company's (check models and names exactly);
- has a comment period or deadline that already passed and creates nothing new;
- is withdrawn or terminated, a meeting or hearing notice, a paperwork/information-collection renewal with no new duty, or a correction that changes nothing material;
- only mentions the company's topic without imposing anything.
Return exactly one decision per document number given — no more, no fewer.

- aml-bsa: AML/BSA program, FinCEN, Travel Rule, SARs
- sanctions: OFAC screening and sanctions compliance
- consumer-payments: Reg E, remittances, prepaid, CFPB supervision, UDAAP

Title: Regulations Regarding Payment of Tax by Commercially Acceptable Means
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: This document contains final regulations regarding the payment of tax by commercially acceptable means. The final regulations reflect changes to the law made by the Taxpayer First Act that would allow the IRS to directly accept payments of tax by credit or debit card, without having to connect taxpayers to third-party payment processors. These final regulations remove restrictions on the payment of any fee by the IRS under any contracts related to payment of taxes by credit, debit, or charge card, and on the IRS imposing any fee or charge on persons paying taxes by credit or debit card.

Change in Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) Approval for Information 
Returns

    Under the PRA, the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) assigned a 
control number to each ``collection of information'' that it reviews 
and approves for use by an agency. A single information collection may 
consist of one or more forms, recordkeeping requirements, and/or third-
party disclosure requirements. Under the PRA and OMB regulations, 
agencies have the discretion to seek separate OMB approvals for forms, 
recordkeeping requirements, and third-party reporting requirements or 
to combine any number of forms, recordkeeping requirements, and/or 
third-party disclosure requirements (usually related in subject matter) 
under one OMB Control Number. Agency decisions on whether to group 
individual requirements under a single OMB Control Number or to 
disaggregate them and request separate OMB Control Numbers are based 
largely on considerations of administrative practicality.
    The PRA also requires agencies to estimate the burden for each 
collection of information. Accordingly, each OMB Control Number has an 
associated burden estimate. The burden estimates for each control 
number are displayed in (1) the PRA notices that accompany collections 
of information, (2) Federal Register notices such as this one, and (3) 
OMB's database of approved information collections. If more than one 
form, recordkeeping requirement, and/or third-party disclosure is 
approved under a single OMB Control Number, the burden estimate for 
that OMB Control Number reflects the burden associated with all the 
approved forms, recordkeeping requirements, and/or third-party 
disclosure requirements.
    As described below under the heading ``Updated Burden Estimate 
Methodology,'' the Internal Revenue Service's (IRS) currently accepted 
burden estimate methodology, referred to as the RAAS Taxpayer Burden 
Model, is based on taxpayers' tax reporting experience taking into 
account, among other things, the forms and schedules used by those 
taxpayers and the recordkeeping and other activities needed to complete 
those forms. The transition of the information return \1\ reporting 
burden represents the IRS's continued effort to improve the ability of 
IRS to measure the burden imposed on various groups of taxpayers by the 
Federal tax system. While the RAAS Taxpayer Burden Model methodology 
provides a more accurate and comprehensive description of information 
return reporting burden, it will not provide burden estimates on a 
form-by-form basis, as has been done under the previous methodology. 
When the prior model, known as the legacy Arthur D. Little (ADL) model 
was developed in the mid-1980s, almost all tax returns were prepared 
manually, either by the taxpayer or a paid preparer. In this context, 
it was determined that estimating burden on a form-by-form, line-by-
line basis was an appropriate methodology. Information returns are 
increasingly being prepared

[[Page 66943]]

using software or with preparer assistance. In this current reporting 
environment, in which many taxpayers' activities are no longer directly 
associated with particular forms, estimating burden on a form-by-form 
basis is not an appropriate method of estimating taxpayer burden. The 
RAAS Taxpayer Burden Model methodology, which takes into account 
broader and more comprehensive taxpayer characteristics and activities, 
provides a much more accurate and useful estimate of taxpayer burden.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \1\ Inclusion or exclusion of forms in this collection is not a 
legal determination that a form is or is not an information return 
as defined by Section 7434. Information return is used here only as 
a general descript of the most prevalent forms by filing numbers 
included in this collection (e.g., Form 1099 and Form 1098).
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Currently, there are 51 forms used by information return issuers 
when complying with Federal tax laws. These include Forms 1098, 1099-B, 
1099-DA, 1099-DIV, 1099-INT, 1099-MISC, 1099-NEC, 1099-R, 5498, W-9 and 
their schedules. For most of these forms, IRS has in the past obtained 
separate OMB approval under unique OMB Control Numbers and separate 
burden estimates.
    The RAAS Taxpayer Burden Model methodology estimates the aggregate 
burden imposed for information reporting, based upon the reporting-
related characteristics and activities of the issuers. IRS therefore 
will seek OMB approval of all 51 information reporting tax forms as a 
single ``collection of information.'' The aggregate burden of these tax 
forms will be accounted for under OMB Control Number 1545-0108, which 
is currently assigned to Form 1096. OMB Control Number 1545-0108 will

AGENCY: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, Treasury.

ACTION: Final rule.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) is issuing 
regulations implementing the Guiding and Establishing National 
Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act regarding the issuance of payment 
stablecoins and certain related activities by entities subject to the 
OCC's jurisdiction.

DATES: The final rule is effective on January 18, 2027.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Sarah Turney, Assistant Director, 
Henry Barkhausen, Special Counsel, Kevin Korzeniewski, Special Counsel, 
Mark O'Horo, Special Counsel, Daniel Borman, Counsel, or Collin Berger, 
Attorney, Chief Counsel's Office, 202-649-5490, Office of the 
Comptroller of the Currency, 400 7th Street SW, Washington, DC 20219. 
If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, please 
dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

I. Background and Summary of the Final Rule

    The Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. 
Stablecoins Act (12 U.S.C. 5901 et seq.) (GENIUS Act or the Act) was 
enacted on July 18, 2025. The Act establishes a regulatory framework 
for payment stablecoin activities.\1\ Stablecoins are digital assets, 
i.e., digital representations of value recorded on a cryptographically 
secured distributed ledger,\2\ such as a blockchain.\3\ The Act sets 
forth various regulatory and licensing requirements for permitted 
payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers. In 
many instances, the Act states that the specific requirements 
applicable to these entities (e.g., those related to capital, 
liquidity, or operational risk management) will be established by 
regulations issued by the relevant primary Federal payment stablecoin 
regulator, in coordination with other relevant agencies, as 
appropriate.\4\ On March 2, 2026, the OCC issued a notice of proposed 
rulemaking (proposal or proposed rule) proposing, and seeking comment 
on, the regulations that would apply to permitted payment stablecoin 
issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers under the OCC's 
jurisdiction (including subsidiaries of insured national banks or 
Federal savings associations, Federal qualified payment stablecoin 
issuers, certain nonbank State qualified payment stablecoin issuers, 
and foreign payment stablecoin issuers) as well as certain custody 
activities conducted by OCC-supervised entities.\5\
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \1\ Under section 2(22) of the Act (12 U.S.C. 5901(22)), 
``payment stablecoin'' means ``a digital asset--(i) that is, or is 
designed to be, used as a means of payment or settlement; and (ii) 
the issuer of which--(I) is obligated to convert, redeem, or 
repurchase for a fixed amount of monetary value, not including a 
digital asset denominated in a fixed amount of monetary value; and 
(II) represents that such issuer will maintain, or create the 
reasonable expectation that it will maintain, a stable value 
relative to the value of a fixed amount of monetary value[.]'' The 
term does not include a digital asset that is (i) a national 
currency; (ii) a deposit (as defined in 12 U.S.C. 1813), including a 
deposit recorded using distributed ledger technology; or (iii) a 
security, as defined in 15 U.S.C. 77b, 78c, or 80a-2.
    \2\ 12 U.S.C. 5901(6).
    \3\ White House, ``Strengthening American Leadership in Digital 
Financial Technology,'' at 15 (July 17, 2025), (hereinafter, Digital 
Financial Technology Report),  https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Digital-Assets-Report-EO14178.pdf . A 
cryptographically secured ledger uses cryptography to maintain the 
integrity of the ledger. See also E.O. No. 14178, Strengthening 
American Leadership in Digital Financial Technology, 90 FR 8647 
(January 31, 2025) (defining blockchain to mean ``any technology 
where data is: (i) shared across a network to create a public ledger 
of verified transactions or information among network participants; 
(ii) linked using cryptography to maintain the integrity of the 
public ledger and to execute other functions; (iii) distributed 
among network participants in an automated fashion to concurrently 
update network participants on the state of the public ledger and 
any other functions; and (iv) composed of source code that is 
publicly available'').
    \4\ See, e.g., 12 U.S.C. 5903(a)(4), (b), (h).
    \5\ See Implementing the Guiding and Establishing National 
Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act for the Issuance of Stablecoins 
by Entities Subject to the Jurisdiction of the Office of the 
Comptroller of the Currency, 91 FR 10202 (March 2, 2026).
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    The OCC received approximately 328 comments in response to the 
proposal from a wide variety of commenters, including crypto-focused 
companies, trade groups, banks, non-profit organizations, academics, 
and individuals.\6\ Commenters had diverging views on several of the 
proposal's key provisions. The final rule addresses these comments, as

Company: Ledgerly Inc.

US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). Small-business invoicing. No lending, no securities brokerage, not a bank.

Rules that APPLY:
- Bank Secrecy Act / AML, FinCEN rules for MSBs, Travel Rule, CVC rules
- OFAC sanctions screening (customers and counterparties, incl. crypto addresses)
- CFPB rules: Reg E (EFTA), remittance rule, prepaid rule, UDAAP, larger-participant rules for payment apps
- Consumer data privacy / GLBA, open banking (1033)
- FTC consumer protection that touches payment apps
- Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
- Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
- CFTC derivatives market rules (DCMs, swaps)
- Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets
- Sanctions actions only matter via the screening program, not individually
